title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When you one-hot encode a categorical variable, each category becomes a separate column. For example, if you have a column with categories {A, B, C}, it will be transformed into three columns: one for each category. Each row will have a $$1$$ in the column corresponding to its category and $$0$$ in others.

title: Intercept Term in the Model
text: Including an intercept term in a model means adding a column of ones to the design matrix. This column accounts for the baseline level of the dependent variable when all other predictors are zero.

title: Columns in the Design Matrix
text: How many columns will the design matrix have after one-hot encoding the 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$ columns and adding an intercept term?

title: Full Column Rank
text: A matrix is full column rank if all its columns are linearly independent. This means no column can be written as a linear combination of the others.

title: Checking Linear Independence
text: Consider the columns created by one-hot encoding. Are any of these columns linearly dependent on others?
